text:
lexa-design: dropped a compact prototype in Figma -> https://figma.com/file/x/rail-zones-proto. Proposal: compress left rail into three sticky zones: Models | Serving | Insights. Goals: reduce vertical noise, clearer entrypoints, and improve deep-link discoverability. feedback? :memo:
ajay-ux: overall 👍. My main concern is discoverability when a deep link targets a nested view (eg. /workspaces/:ws/models/:id?open=versions). should the app land on the nested panel directly or open the group then focus into the nested tab? which pattern feels more consistent for back-button + bookmarking?
sam-frontend: i propose canonical nested URLs (so everything is bookmarkable). client behavior: when loaded, expand parent, scroll into view, then move focus into the nested panel heading. implementation note: we should add a minimal query param behaviour: ?open=versions to indicate tab; otherwise default to first tab. sample routes i'm imagining:
/workspaces/:ws/models/:modelId
/workspaces/:ws/models/:modelId?open=versions
/workspaces/:ws/serve/instances/:instId
/workspaces/:ws/insights/usage
kelly-pm: taxonomy reminder: let's standardize on the word "Models" (not "Model Registry") across the console and docs. breadcrumbs should be human readable: "My Workspace > Models > MyModel" not raw path segments. also: can we include a small permalink copy affordance on rows so PMs can share exact model links?
mike-a11y: a11y notes: when we programmatically expand a rail group, we must announce that to screen readers with aria-live (polite). suggested phrasing: "Models expanded, 5 items". also group headers need role="button", aria-expanded toggles, and keyboard operability (space/enter to toggle). when deep-link opens a nested panel, move focus to the panel heading (role="heading" + tabindex=\"-1\") and call focus() so AT reads it. ensure focus outline is visible for keyboard users.
tara-research: from user testing, participants expected back to reliably return them to previous scroll position in the list. if we push a client-side nav, include history state with scrollY. users get confused when list resets to top on back.
sam-frontend: implementation sketch: on navigate to detail, do history.pushState({scroll: window.scrollY, open: currentTab}, '', href); on popstate, if state.scroll present, restore scroll and collapse states accordingly. we need tests for direct loads vs in-app nav and SSR fallbacks.
kelly-pm: small copy nit: the chevrons on group headers currently read "open" and "close" in title attr. change to "Expand Models" / "Collapse Models" for clarity. also permalink tooltip should say "Copy link to model".
mike-a11y: permalink must be keyboard focusable and have an accessible name. color contrast: ensure icon hit target at least 24px and contrast >= 4.5:1 or provide visible focus ring.
routebot: route-lint-bot: failing specs: history-restore.test.js for /workspaces/:ws/models flow. CI job #4539.
lexa-design: action items: 1) sam to open PR with history-state + unit tests. 2) mike to write detailed a11y acceptance criteria (aria-live strings, focus targets, keyboard). 3) design to update Figma copy to "Models" and adjust chevrons/aria-expanded. 4) research to add a small test case for back-button scroll recovery. 5) eng infra to triage the CI failures. i'll create GH issues and link them here. thanks all! :party_parrot:
